newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Evergreen approves issue of 33 mln shrs.
newsitem.headline: Evergreen approves issue of 33 mln shrs.

text.p: The shareholders of listed forest owner Evergreen Forests on Tuesday approved an issue of 33 million shares to help fund the purchase of Fletcher Challenge's South Auckland forests.

The company previously announced that it planned to fund the NZ$30 million purchase in part by a placement of 33 million shares at 55.5 cents mainly to United States institutions and by an increase in the company's existing capitalised term loan facility.
Chief executive Mark Bogle said subscriptions had exceeded the company's target and had resulted in a good spread of international institutions, particularly from the U.S., taking up the offer.

Last week Societe Generale Asset Management said it had extended its relevant interest in Evergreen to 12.9 percent, through a conditional agreement to take up 12 million shares through the placement.

Bogle said the level of interest reflected both a growing appreciation of the need for plantation forestry to meet the world's growing demands for wood, and the advantages of New Zealand as one of about three regions in the world where wood growing could generate a an acceptable return on capital.
He said interest was reinforced by the recent move by U.S. forestry giant Weyerhaeuser to buy an operating stake in a Nelson forestry partnership from Fletcher Challenge.
Coupled with the activities of US interests International Paper and Rayonier, the Weyerhaeuser move was "very positive" for the local industry.
"It means that radiata (pine) is becoming part of the global marketing strategy of the major international timber companies."
